transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands — Leadership Update
Date: 2026-06-25 | Start: 17:00 UTC | Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Evan Ross, Priya Singh, Miguel Alvarez, Hannah Lee, Zoe Carter, Rajesh Kumar, Olivia Park, Marcos Diaz + company-wide audience

Summary: Quick leadership updates across GTM, engineering, product, and security. Celebrate Q2 milestones (Hosted revenue +16% QoQ), call out Dedicated deal wins, and align on SOC 2 timeline and Q3 product launches. Several action items assigned.

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone welcome, thanks for joining, I know it's end of quarter for many teams so we'll run through a compressed agenda, um, high level Q2 performance then product and ops.
[00:18] Evan: Quick shout out — huge thanks to sales and success, we closed two Dedicated contracts this month that push us into new mid-market territory, im pretty proud of the cross-functional push on those.
[00:35] Rajesh: Yeah those were multi-week cycles; shout to engineering for the POC support and to Olivia for pulling security docs for procurement.
[00:50] Priya: I'll share a short hiring update, we ve opened 18 new reqs across infra, platform and go-to-market; please prioritize interviews for top candidates this week, otherwise we'll lose momentum.
[01:12] Miguel: On infra — latency improvements in the runtime are looking good; our internal benchmark shows median p50 token latency for standard chat workload down 12% after kernel selection changes. There's still noisy tails at high concurrency, Zoe and I are vetting some batching heuristics.
[01:35] Zoe: Right, the continuous batching adjustments help cost but we have to keep an eye on cold-starts for small requests, we're experimenting with a hybrid warmpool. Note the numbers are from staging and may be optimistic versus customer traffic.
[01:55] Hannah: Product roadmap — Q3 will focus on three launches: 1) streaming assist improvements + tool-calling reliability, 2) private deployment quickstart (VPC templates + kube operator), and 3) Optimize recommendations UI in the console. We'll publish a more granular timeline.
[02:15] Evan: On the private deployment quickstart — this was a frequent ask from enterprise trials, gives them a lower friction path to VPC and air-gapped installs. Miguel, estimate for GA?
[02:30] Miguel: If we keep the current sprint cadence and no major blockers, early GA late Q3, but that's contingent on the operator stability work and some infra automation.
[02:42] Priya: A note on Q2 metrics — hosted API revenue +16% QoQ, embedding usage continues to drive stickiness. We saw a small uptick in churn for a few smaller customers tied to cost sensitivity; the Optimize tooling is already helping but Sales should flag price-sensitivity earlier.
[03:08] Rajesh: We're refining the playbook for cost talk — showing batching and quantization recommendations reduces sticker shock; next week we'll run enablement for AE's using the Optimize dashboard.
[03:30] Olivia: Security update — SOC 2 readiness: we're about 65% through the gap remediation list. Key items outstanding: rotate certain service account keys into KMS, finalize RBAC for private installs, and complete retention policy enforcement. Expect formal auditor readiness by end of Q3.
[03:55] Evan: Thanks Olivia, that's a priority for enterprise. Any blockers that need exec support?
[04:03] Olivia: We need dedicated infra hours for the key-rotation automation and a small cross-team working group — two sprints should close the biggest gaps.
[04:15] Priya: We'll allocate the hours, planning to reassign two infra engineers for the next three weeks.
[04:24] Marcos: On customers — success has has been running more technical benchmarks with two pilot accounts on Dedicated; both reported >30% cost improvement vs naive self-hosting and similar latency to hosted when using our autoscaling profiles. I'll circulate the benchmark summaries.
[04:45] Evan: Great, those benchmarks are going to be crucial for mid-market sales. Make sure we capture methodology and raw data.
[04:57] Marcos: Yep, raw data + benchmarking script will go to the shared drive, note that some numbers are noisy because customers ran mixed workloads.
[05:10] [Audience question] Participant (unnamed): Any update on EMEA regions? latency?
[05:18] Priya: We're on track to add one more cloud region in EMEA in Q3; that will help latency for EU customers and support data residency asks.
[05:30] Miguel: Region rollout includes region-aware routing in the control plane and capacity planning for Dedicated pools. We're building in smart routing rules to failover gracefully.
[05:45] Hannah: Also, marketing will push a product brief on regional availability to help SDRs.
[06:00] Evan: Ok let's talk hiring briefly — org chart update: we have three ICs moving to staff level, congratulate them — and an open request to increase headcount in infra by two. Priya?
[06:15] Priya: Yes, comp and hiring note: compensation band refresh is happening next month — we'll share details in the compensation doc. Also parental leave policy update will be posted.
[06:30] Zoe: Engineering cadence — post-Q2 we'll throttle down non-critical roadmap work for two weeks to focus on debt and reliability. Please surface anything you think is critical.
[06:45] Miguel: On technical debt — the KV cache consistency work still needs more testing, it's causing occasional session regressions in heavy writes. We'll hold a deep-dive with affected teams.
[07:00] Hannah: Product question from the chat — "When will function-calling be available in Dedicated?" Miguel: We're targeting function-calling in Dedicated by the end of Q3, initial support will be alpha with limited kernel optimizations.
[07:20] [08:00] Evan: Finance snapshot — burn rate is tracking to plan; runway unchanged post Series C, revenue acceleration is the lever. Priya will share exact numbers to managers.
[08:12] Priya: I'll send the Q2 financials to managers by Monday.
[08:24] Rajesh: Partner updates — we've added two ISV partners to the marketplace pilot, and one partner integration simplified private deploy onboarding. We'll share the partner list.
[08:40] Evan: A couple of product-pricing notes: we will pilot a new committed-rate plan for Dedicated customers that smooths cost and gives better unit economics for high-throughput workloads. More details soon.
[09:02] Olivia: Compliance question from legal — data residency for EU customers and audit logging retention, we need to finalize retention windows. Suggestion: default 90 days with an enterprise option.
[09:20] Hannah: From a UX perspective, we can surface retention as a configurable field in the Console and document implications.
[09:34] [10:00] Evan: Open mic — quick wins, shoutouts — shout to the infra on the batch improvements, shout to Sales on the Dedicated renewals, shout to Docs for the new quickstart guides.
[10:20] [11:00] Evan: Ok last section — Q&A and closing. A question in the chat: "Are we changing our go-to-market focus?" Rajesh: Not shifting — still PLG-led but we'll be more targeted with an enterprise overlay where usage hits thresholds.
[11:35] Evan: Final reminders — fill out the NPS follow-up for Q2, participate in the onboarding refresher if you're mentoring new hires, and expect the roadmap email tomorrow.
[11:50] Evan: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.

Action items (recap):
- Priya: Comp and hiring doc — circulate by 2026-06-29.
- Miguel & Zoe: Deep-dive on KV cache consistency and batching tails; deliver notes and benchmark links by 2026-07-06.
- Olivia: SOC 2 gap analysis + remediation dates — publish by 2026-07-02.
- Marcos: Benchmark data and methodology upload — due 2026-06-28.

References mentioned: internal benchmark spreadsheet (link shared in chat), SOC 2 readiness checklist (docs repo), private deploy quickstart draft (confluence).

Notes on transcription: auto-generated notes with occasional name recognition errors, punctuation inconsistent, some speaker attribution uses job titles rather than exact names.
